title: Organic vs conventional farming crop yield gap
research_question: How much lower is crop yield under organic farming compared to conventional farming?

population.description: Crop plants grown in field experiments comparing farming systems

intervention.description: Organic farming system (certified organic or following organic principles: no synthetic fertilizers, no synthetic pesticides)

comparator.description: Conventional farming system (using synthetic fertilizers and/or pesticides)
comparator.definition: Conventional management with synthetic inputs allowed, serving as the high-input reference

primary.description: Crop yield (grain, fruit, or total biomass harvested per unit area)

intervention: Organic farming (no synthetic fertilizers or pesticides)
primary_outcomes: Crop yield (grain, fruit, or harvested biomass per hectare)
typical_effect_size: -19% to -25% yield gap (organic lower than conventional)
important_moderators: Crop type (cereal, legume, fruit, vegetable, oilseed, root/tuber)
Crop species (wheat, maize, rice, soybean, tomato, potato, etc.)
Experiment type (long-term trial, on-farm comparison, field trial)
extraction_priorities: 1. CRITICAL: Extract EVERY crop-year combination separately
2. Treatment = ORGANIC system; Control = CONVENTIONAL system
3. If multiple crops compared, extract EACH crop as separate observation
4. Get variance (SE/SD/LSD) and sample size (n) for meta-analysis weighting
5. Record crop species and study duration
6. Convert all yields to consistent units (prefer kg/ha or Mg/ha)
tc_confusion_warnings: Treatment is ORGANIC (lower input), Control is CONVENTIONAL (higher input)
Some papers compare 3+ systems (organic, integrated, conventional) - extract organic vs conventional only
Low-input is NOT the same as organic unless explicitly stated
Transitional organic may show different effects than established organic - record years since conversion
Watch for factorial designs (organic x irrigation) - extract each organic vs conventional at same irrigation level

search.seed_papers_description: Ponisio et al. 2015 (meta-analysis, Proc R Soc B), Seufert et al. 2012 (Nature), de Ponti et al. 2012 (Agric Syst)

inclusion_criteria: Primary field experiment comparing organic and conventional systems
Organic system prohibits synthetic fertilizers and pesticides
Conventional system uses standard synthetic inputs
exclusion_criteria: No true conventional control (only organic vs organic)
Only economic or environmental comparison without yield data

benchmark.source: Ponisio et al. 2015 (Proc R Soc B 282:20141396)
